functional.title: Functional self-test
functional.subtitle: Create two folders in your personal space, ingest a marker document into one and a plain document into the other, then ask the real self-test agent a question scoped to each — the marker must come back from the first and be absent from the second. Everything is cleaned up at the end.

web.title: Web research self-test
web.subtitle: Run the deterministic web research agent through the real execution pipeline. It fails first when web research is not enabled on this deployment; otherwise it proves each protection holds — refused schemes, ports and credentials, loopback, private, metadata and encoded addresses, platform service names, redirects to internal destinations, binary content, and a SafeSearch the model cannot weaken — then that search and page reading work. Probes that need an unreachable third-party endpoint are skipped, never passed. The temporary agent is deleted at the end.

authz.identityDescription: Checks authenticated access to the three APIs, rejection of missing or invalid tokens, public routes and personal-space identity. Checks that do not apply to this provider are skipped with a reason.
authz.title: Authorization self-test
authz.subtitle: Proves the live API honors the authorization model: platform-admin flags match real endpoint access, and nobody — not even a platform admin — gets implicit access to a team they don't belong to.

expiry.caption: Uses your current SSO session. The agent checks authenticated metadata access, waits past the captured token's expiry, then repeats the check. No password, Keycloak configuration change, document, or library is needed. Only a temporary agent instance is created and removed; closing the tab mid-run leaves it behind, to delete from your personal agents. Browser refresh stays enabled. The wait is the token's remaining lifetime plus a short margin — from under a minute to several — so keep this page open until it ends; a wait longer than {{maxMinutes}} minutes is skipped.

search.hybridDescription: Hybrid search combines keyword matching (exact terms, names, IDs) with semantic similarity. It is the best option when your question contains specific terminology (component names, error codes, APIs) but also benefits from conceptual matching. Hybrid typically improves recall while keeping precision high, at the cost of slightly more computation.
search.semanticDescription: Semantic search uses embeddings to retrieve passages that are conceptually similar to your question, even if they don't share the same words. This usually finds the most relevant context for broad or exploratory questions, but it can sometimes include loosely related results when your query is very short or ambiguous.
search.strictDescription: Strict search prioritizes precision over coverage. It applies tighter constraints (e.g., stronger keyword/metadata matching and/or higher similarity thresholds) so only highly confident results are retrieved. Use this when you want to avoid ‘maybe relevant' documents, or when your corpus is large and you prefer fewer, more exact sources. If nothing matches strongly, results may be sparse.
